title: Surgeon visit
what: A doctor who decides if you need surgery and treats conditions that surgery can help, from hernias to abscesses.
why: For a hernia, gallstones, an abscess, an ingrown nail, lumps under the skin, or before planned surgery.
tell_doctor: What bothers you, and since when
All your medicines, especially blood thinners
Past surgeries and how you handled anesthesia
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring ultrasounds, scans, and test results, if you had them.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that makes it easy to show the area.

bring: Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
The area is examined and felt
The doctor explains if surgery is needed and what the options are
If surgery is needed, you get a list of pre-op tests
feel: Feeling the sore area may be unpleasant
Tell the doctor if it hurts
after: If surgery is needed, the doctor will tell you how to prepare
red_flags: Severe belly pain, vomiting, or a high fever: do not wait for the visit. Call emergency services

faq.q: Will surgery be scheduled right away?
faq.a: Not always. Often tests come first, and sometimes surgery is not needed at all.

faq.q: What should I ask the surgeon?
faq.a: What the treatment options are, the risks, how long recovery takes, and when you can work.

reminders.text: Surgeon visit tomorrow. Bring your test results and medicine list.
